title: What are you into?
goals: Talk about your interests and skills with can, like, love, hate, prefer, enjoy, and would like.
Use the right verb form: to + verb, verb + -ing, or the base form.
Talk about music and likes using object pronouns (me, him, her, it, us, them).
Use everybody, everyone, nobody, and no one with a singular verb.
Say no politely (Not really, Well, no...) and use really to strengthen or soften.
Connect ideas in writing with and, also, especially, or, but, and because.

learn.title: Likes and skills: can, like, enjoy, would like, good at
learn.html:
After certain verbs, the next verb changes form. Memorize each group:

StructureExamples
can / can't + base verbI can play the piano. / I can't swim.
love, like, hate, prefer + to + verb or verb + -ing (same meaning)I love to swim. = I love swimming.
I prefer to watch TV. = I prefer watching TV.
would like + to + verb (only this way)Would you like to play jazz? / I'd like to play jazz.
enjoy + verb + -ing (only this way)I enjoy writing.
preposition + verb + -ing (good at, interested in, excited about)I'm good at drawing people. / I'm not interested in skiing.
  • Questions: Can you draw? / Do you like to cook? / Would you like to join? / Are you good at cooking?
  • I'd like = I would like. It is not the same as I like.
  • A verb in -ing can be an object: I hate doing homework.

watch.wrong: I'd like going to a concert.
watch.right: I'd like to go to a concert.
watch.why: Would like goes with to + verb.

watch.wrong: I'm good at play the guitar.
watch.right: I'm good at playing the guitar.

learn.title: Object pronouns and everybody / nobody
learn.html:
When a person or thing receives the action, you use the object pronoun. It goes after the verb or after a preposition.

SubjectIyouhesheitwethey
Objectmeyouhimheritusthem
  • I don't like him. / Do you like them? / That's me on the CD.
  • With a preposition: Come and listen to us. / I listen to it all the time.

everybody / everyone = all people. nobody / no one = no person. With these subjects, the verb goes in the third person singular:

  • Everybody likes pop. / Everyone in my class loves her.
  • Nobody is a jazz fan. / No one listens to country.

Nobody and no one are already negative: don't add don't / doesn't.

watch.why: After the verb, use the object pronoun: her.
After a preposition, use an object pronoun.
Nobody is already negative: no double negative.

learn.title: Connecting ideas: and, also, especially, or, but, because
learn.html:
These words connect ideas and make your text sound natural.

WordUseExample
andaddingI enjoy knitting and I make cool hats.
alsoadding (before the verb; after be)I also like making jewelry. / I'm also good at cooking.
especiallyhighlightingI like sports, especially football.
oroptions; negativesDo you prefer pop or rock? / I'm not interested in running or jogging.
butcontrastI'm not good at sports, but I want to do something outdoors.
becausegiving a reasonMy friends love my hats because they are unique.
  • In negative sentences, use or, not and: I don't like pop or rock.
  • After because, use a complete sentence (subject + verb).

watch.wrong: I don't like pop and rock.
watch.right: I don't like pop or rock.
watch.why: In negatives, use or to connect options.

watch.wrong: I like jazz because is relaxing.
watch.right: I like jazz because it's relaxing.

watch.wrong: I also am good at drawing.
I like all sports, specially football.
watch.right: I like all sports, especially football.

learn.title: Saying no politely and using really
learn.html:
In English, a flat “No” sounds rude. To say no politely, add something more: an explanation or an alternative.

QuestionPolite answer
Do you do a lot of cooking?Not really.
Do you collect anything?Um, no. I'm not really into collecting things.
Do you play golf?No, I don't, but I play tennis a lot.
Do you have a lot of hobbies?Well, no. I don't really have much time.

Really changes how strong the sentence is:

  • It makes the idea stronger before a positive verb or adjective: I really love riding my horse. / I'm really good at photography.
  • It makes it softer in negatives: I don't really have much time. / I'm not really interested in sports.
  • Not really works as a polite answer to a yes/no question.

reading.title: What are you into? The Hobby Corner
reading.intro: Read the forum messages and answer.
paragraphs: Welcome to the Hobby Corner, an online forum for people with interesting free time. This week's question is: "What are you into?" Here are three messages from our members.

Rita: Hi, everyone! I'm from Monterrey and I love knitting. I make some really cool hats, and my friends love wearing them because they're unique. I also like making jewelry, especially bracelets. I'm not good at sports, but I want to do something outdoors. Can you recommend a hobby?

Jon: I play the saxophone in a small jazz band with my cousins, and my sister is the lead singer. Everybody in my family likes music, but nobody in my class listens to jazz! We'd like to play at the local talent show next month. Come and listen to us if you can.

Lucy: Honestly, I'm not really into hobbies. I don't really have much time because I work full-time. I like cooking, but I don't cook every day. Sometimes I play board games with my roommates on Sundays, and I enjoy doing crossword puzzles on the bus. Do you have any easy hobbies for busy people?

Moderator: Thanks for your messages! Rita, try hiking or cycling with a local club. Jon, good luck at the talent show. Lucy, why don't you join a small book club? You only need one hour a week, and everybody there is very friendly.

We have a concert on Saturday. Come and listen to us!
